blocks.name: Horizontal Scroll
blocks.cardDesc: A reusable WordPress component that turns normal scrolling into animated stories using images with text notes on the images to explain what’s going on as a user scrolls.
blocks.tagline: A reusable WordPress component that turns normal scrolling into animated stories using images with text notes on the images to explain what’s going on as a user scrolls.
blocks.definition: A reusable WordPress component that turns normal scrolling into animated stories using images with text notes on top of the images to explain what's going on as a user scrolls.
blocks.howItWorks: You scroll down the page like normal, but instead of the image just disappearing off screen, it slides sideways. Text (a title and a short description) are rightfully positioned on the image parts to label what the user is looking at.
whatIsExpected: You upload one or more images, and the block stitches them together into one long strip.
As you scroll down, the strip sticks to the screen instead of scrolling away.
While it's stuck, your scrolling slides the strip sideways.
Once you've scrolled through the whole strip, the page goes back to scrolling normally.
Text notes float above the image and appear as their part of the image comes into view.
whatShouldBeProvided: Image parts that make up the long strip.
Text notes on each image (title, body, horizontal position, vertical position, width and styles).

howToUse.detail: Insert the Horizontal Scrolly block from the block panel.

howToUse.title: Upload & position image
howToUse.detail: Upload an image, add alt text and set position (left, right, center).

howToUse.title: Add text note
howToUse.detail: A title, body text, position, and style.

howToUse.title: Repeat per image
howToUse.detail: Do this for every image that makes up the strip.

howToUse.title: Preview
howToUse.detail: Check how it looks, or go back and edit.

howToUse.title: Save
howToUse.detail: Save the block.

whereToUse: A journey through a physical space — e.g. a market, a city.
A before and after that unfolds gradually.
Any sequence with a clear left to right order.
blocks.caution: Skip it for stories with heavy body text — the format favors a handful of strong images over paragraphs.

examples.headline: Jollof Road series
A Lagos car crash almost killed him. A €900 visa saved his dream of seeing the world.

blocks.name: Scroll Swap
blocks.cardDesc: This is a design technique where one visual element seamlessly replaces another as the user scrolls through the page. Here, a writer can use more than one image or a video to tell a story
blocks.tagline: This is a design technique where one visual element seamlessly replaces another as the user scrolls through the page. Here, a writer can use more than one image or a video to tell a story
blocks.definition: A reusable WordPress component that turns normal scrolling into an animated story by scrolling between images vertically as the reader scrolls, with text notes labelling each moment.
blocks.howItWorks: You scroll down the page like normal, and the current image scrolls upward and out of view while the next image slides up to take its place — the same directional motion as normal page scrolling, just applied to the image itself. Text (a title and a short description) label each image as it appears.
whatIsExpected: You upload two or more images, each becoming one step in the sequence.
As you scroll down, the frame sticks to the screen instead of scrolling away.
Further scrolling moves the current image upward and out of view, while the next image slides up to replace it.
Once you've scrolled through every image, the page goes back to scrolling normally.
Text notes appear over each image as it comes into view.
whatShouldBeProvided: Image parts that make up the sequence.
Text notes on each image (title, body, position, and style).

howToUse.title: Insert block
howToUse.detail: Insert the Scroll Swap block from the block panel.

howToUse.title: Upload & position image
howToUse.detail: Upload an image, add alt text and set position (left, right, center).

howToUse.title: Add text note
howToUse.detail: A title, body text, position, and style.

howToUse.title: Repeat per swap step
howToUse.detail: Do this for every image in the sequence.

howToUse.title: Preview
howToUse.detail: Check how it looks, or go back and edit.

howToUse.title: Save
howToUse.detail: Save the block.

whereToUse: Before-and-after comparisons.
A short series of distinct moments or stages.
Contrasting two or more scenes without needing a continuous strip.
blocks.caution: Avoid it for content that needs images to overlap or blend — swaps replace one image with the next rather than merging them.

examples.headline: #NairaLife: This 26-Year-Old Built a ₦7.9 Million Safety Net in 2 Years. How?
What ₦100,000 in Nigeria's biggest bank stocks became in 8 months

blocks.name: Ken Burns
blocks.cardDesc: This is a scrolling effect that slowly pans across and zooms in or out of a still photograph to bring it to life.
blocks.tagline: This is a scrolling effect that slowly pans across and zooms in or out of a still photograph to bring it to life.
blocks.definition: A reusable WordPress component that turns normal scrolling into an animated story by starting zoomed in on a chosen focal point and zooming out as the reader scrolls, revealing the full image, with text notes labelling what's being highlighted.
blocks.howItWorks: You scroll down the page like normal, but instead of the image moving away, it starts zoomed in tight on a point you've chosen and slowly zooms out, revealing more of the image as you scroll. Text (a title and a short description) can label what's being highlighted as it zooms.
whatIsExpected: You upload one or more images, each becoming one zoom step.
As you scroll down, the frame sticks to the screen instead of scrolling away.
The image starts zoomed in on its set focal point, and further scrolling zooms it out to reveal the full image.
Once you've scrolled through every zoom step, the page goes back to scrolling normally.
Text notes appear over each part as it comes into view.
whatShouldBeProvided: Image parts that make up the zoom sequence.
An X/Y focal point and zoom size for each part.
Text notes on each image (title, body, position, and style).

howToUse.title: Insert block
howToUse.detail: Insert the Ken Burns block from the block panel.

howToUse.title: Upload & position image
howToUse.detail: Upload an image, add alt text and set position (left, right, center).

howToUse.title: Set zoom
howToUse.detail: Set the X/Y focal point and starting zoom-in level, which zooms out on scroll.

howToUse.title: Add text note
howToUse.detail: A title, body text, position, and style.

howToUse.title: Repeat per zoom part
howToUse.detail: Do this for every part in the sequence.

howToUse.title: Preview & save
howToUse.detail: Check how it looks, then save the block.

whereToUse: Maps where a specific location needs highlighting.
Documents or screenshots where one detail matters most.
Scenes where the real story lives in a small part of a larger image.
blocks.caution: Avoid it for images without an obvious focal point — the zoom will feel arbitrary rather than purposeful.

examples.headline: Ayodele Adio Has A Plan To Fix Lagos' Rent Problem
Schneider Electric says Africa's electricity grid is the next AI battleground

blocks.name: Article Page
blocks.cardDesc: The standard layout for a single story: Title, byline, hero image, body and related image
blocks.tagline: The standard layout for a single story: Title, byline, hero image, body and related image
blocks.definition: A reusable WordPress page template that lays out a single story consistently across the site: a title, author and date, a hero or feature image, the article body, and related stories at the end.
blocks.howItWorks: When a writer publishes a story, WordPress renders it into this fixed structure automatically — the title and byline sit at the top, followed by a feature image, then the article body, and a set of related stories at the bottom to keep readers on the site.
whatIsExpected: The title displays prominently at the top of the page.
The author's name and publish date appear directly beneath the title.
A hero or feature image sits above the article body, giving the story a strong visual anchor.
The article content flows below in the standard body layout.
A related stories section appears at the end, pulling in similar articles to keep readers engaged.
whatShouldBeProvided: Author byline and publish date (usually automatic).
Tags or category assignment, so related stories surface correctly.

howToUse.detail: Add the story's headline as the page title.

howToUse.title: Set feature image
howToUse.detail: Upload the hero image for the top of the page.

howToUse.title: Write body
howToUse.detail: Add the full article content.

howToUse.title: Assign category
howToUse.detail: So related stories surface correctly.

howToUse.title: Preview
howToUse.detail: Check how the layout reads end-to-end.

howToUse.title: Publish
howToUse.detail: Publish the story.

whereToUse: Any standard news, feature, or interview story.
Long-form pieces that benefit from a strong hero image up top.
Any content meant to funnel readers into more site content via related stories.
blocks.caution: This is the default template for most stories — reach for the Listing or Form pattern instead when the page isn't a single story.

MTN controls 55% of Nigeria's fibre market, but the overall sector remains tiny

blocks.name: Listing Page
blocks.cardDesc: A scannable grid of story cards, grouped by categories for homepages
blocks.tagline: A scannable grid of story cards, grouped by categories for homepages
blocks.definition: A reusable WordPress page template that displays multiple stories at once as a scannable list or grid, used for homepages, category pages, and topic collections.
blocks.howItWorks: Instead of one story, this template pulls in many stories at once and displays each as a compact card: a thumbnail image, a category tag, a headline, the author, and the date. Cards are grouped by category, usually with a “see more” or “load more” link at the end of each section.
whatIsExpected: Each story appears as a card with a thumbnail image, category tag, headline, author, and date.
Cards are grouped into sections by category or topic.
Each section ends with a “see more” or “load more” link to the full category page.
The newest stories typically appear first within each section.
whatShouldBeProvided: A thumbnail image for each story.
A category or tag assignment for grouping.
A defined number of stories per section, and a link to the full category archive.

howToUse.title: Publish
howToUse.detail: Publish the page.

whereToUse: Homepages that need to surface many stories at once.
Category or topic archive pages.
Collection pages grouping stories around a theme.
blocks.caution: Keep card copy (headline, tag) concise — this pattern is built for scanning quickly, not reading in place.

examples.headline: Homepage — sectioned by vertical (Startups, FinTech, Banking, Companies, Features, News, TC Insights)
Homepage — latest content grid plus category archive links

blocks.name: Full Width Hero Block
blocks.cardDesc: A page treatment where the hero or feature image stretches across 100% of the viewport width, rather than being boxed within the article's content column.
blocks.tagline: A page treatment where the hero or feature image stretches across 100% of the viewport width, rather than being boxed within the article's content column.
blocks.definition: A page pattern where the story's hero image spans the full width of the browser viewport (100% width, edge to edge), rather than being constrained to the article's text column, giving flagship feature stories a more immersive opening.
blocks.howItWorks: Instead of sitting inside the article's normal content width, the hero image breaks out to fill the entire browser window from edge to edge. The headline, byline, and category tag sit directly below the image before the article body returns to its normal contained width.
whatIsExpected: The hero image loads first, above the headline, category tag, and byline.
The image stretches to fill the entire browser viewport width, with no side margins.
The headline, category tag, and byline sit directly below the image, back in the normal contained width.
The rest of the article body continues in the standard contained width.
whatShouldBeProvided: A high-resolution hero image or GIF suited to a full-width, edge-to-edge crop.
The story's category tag, title, byline, and date, which render below the image.
The rest of the article content as normal.

howToUse.title: Insert block
howToUse.detail: Add it at the very top of the article.

howToUse.title: Upload hero image
howToUse.detail: Use a high-resolution image built for an edge-to-edge crop.

howToUse.title: Add title & byline
howToUse.detail: These render below the full-width image.

howToUse.title: Continue with body
howToUse.detail: Write the rest of the article as normal below the hero.

howToUse.title: Preview
howToUse.detail: Check the image spans the full viewport on desktop and mobile.

howToUse.title: Publish
howToUse.detail: Publish the story.

whereToUse: High-impact feature stories or investigations that benefit from a strong visual opening.
Stories with a striking, wide-format image or GIF.
Not needed for standard news or shorter pieces — reserve it for flagship features.
blocks.caution: A full-width hero is a visual statement — using it on every story dilutes its impact. Reserve it for genuine flagship features.

examples.headline: Inside the spam call machine behind Nigeria's digital lending boom

blocks.name: Page Category Block
blocks.cardDesc: A collection page with one central story up top and a numbered list of related stories below with a read story button below
blocks.tagline: A collection page with one central story up top and a numbered list of related stories below with a read story button below
blocks.definition: A page pattern used for collections or event coverage, combining one central, featured story at the top with a numbered list of every other related story in the series, each rendered as its own card with a headline, short description, and a “Read Story” button.
blocks.howItWorks: The page opens with an introduction to the collection and a central, featured story. Below that, every other story in the series is listed in order, each as its own short card: a headline, a one- or two-line description, and a distinctly colored “Read Story” button linking out to the full piece.
whatIsExpected: An introduction at the top explains what the collection is and its scope (e.g. an event, a themed series).
One central or featured story is highlighted prominently near the top.
Every other story in the collection is listed below, numbered in order.
Each story in the list shows a headline, a short description, and a “Read Story” button.
Clicking “Read Story” takes the reader to that story's full article page.
whatShouldBeProvided: The central or featured story to highlight.
A headline and short description for every other story in the series.
A link to each story's full article.

howToUse.detail: Add it for the collection's landing page.

howToUse.detail: Introduce the collection and its scope.

Themed series or year-end collections (e.g. predictions, retrospectives).
Any topic where readers benefit from browsing many related pieces from one hub page.
blocks.caution: Keep each story's description short — this page is a hub for browsing, not a place to read full content.

blocks.tagline: An intro block combining a small eyebrow label, a bold headline, and a short description paragraph, used to open a case study or platform overview.
blocks.definition: A case study block that introduces a platform, event, or initiative with a small uppercase eyebrow label, a large bold headline, and a short description paragraph beneath it.
blocks.howItWorks: The writer sets a short eyebrow label (like “THE PLATFORM”) above a bold, attention-grabbing headline, followed by a paragraph explaining the context in more detail.
whatIsExpected: A small, muted eyebrow label appears above the headline (e.g. “THE PLATFORM”).
A large, bold headline follows, stating the key fact or claim.
A description paragraph beneath the headline adds context and detail.

sponsorship pages published as a page.

blocks.name: Stats Grid

blocks.tagline: A grid of bold statistics, each paired with a short label, used to summarise key results at a glance.
blocks.definition: A case study block that displays a set of key figures as a grid, each cell showing one bold number and a short label beneath it, colored to visually separate each stat.
blocks.howItWorks: Each cell in the grid shows one large number and a short label underneath, colored with a distinct pastel background so each stat stands out and the grid stays scannable.
whatIsExpected: Each cell shows one large, bold number.
A short label appears beneath each number, explaining what it measures.
Cells are arranged in a grid, typically 3 columns, and can span multiple rows.
Each cell has a distinct background color to visually separate the stats.

A short label for each stat.

sponsorship pages, showing impact figures to potential partners.

blocks.name: Case Study Quote

blocks.tagline: A quote or key insight set apart with a colored left border and a light background panel, distinct from the large-quotation-mark Pull Quote used in articles.
blocks.definition: A case study block that highlights a key quote or insight using a colored left border and a light background panel, rather than the large quotation-mark styling used in article Pull Quotes.
blocks.howItWorks: The writer places a short, important line of text into the block, which renders with a colored accent bar on the left and a light background, setting it apart from surrounding paragraphs without decorative quotation marks.
whatIsExpected: A colored vertical bar appears on the left edge of the block.
The quote or insight text sits inside a light background panel.
The styling is simpler than the article Pull Quote — no large quotation mark.
whatShouldBeProvided: An accent color for the left border, usually matching the case study's branding.

blocks.tagline: A horizontally scrollable gallery of images or GIFs, introduced by a short caption, used to showcase moments from an event or campaign.

blocks.howItWorks: A short caption sets up the context (e.g. “Main Stage conversations and speaker-audience interaction”), followed by a row of images the reader can scroll through horizontally to see more.
whatIsExpected: A short caption appears above the image row, describing the moment or theme.
Images or GIFs are arranged in a horizontal row, with more visible by scrolling sideways.
Images can be photos or GIFs, depending on the moment being shown.

blocks.name: Quotes
blocks.cardDesc: A native WordPress block that lets writers pull a short, striking line out of the article and display it in a larger, distinct style.
blocks.tagline: A native WordPress block that lets writers pull a short, striking line out of the article and display it in a larger, distinct style.
blocks.definition: The Pull Quote block is a native WordPress block that highlights a short, impactful line from the article as a large, styled quote, pulling the reader's eye to it distinctly from the surrounding body text.
blocks.howItWorks: The writer adds the Pull Quote block at the point in the article where a line deserves emphasis. WordPress renders it in a larger, distinct style, set apart from the paragraph text around it, with an optional citation underneath.
whatIsExpected: The writer places the block at the point in the article where a line should stand out.
The quote renders in a larger, distinct style, separate from the surrounding paragraph text.
An optional citation can appear beneath the quote to credit the speaker or source.

howToUse.title: Add quote text
howToUse.detail: Type or paste the line you want to highlight.

howToUse.title: Add citation
howToUse.detail: Optional — credit the speaker or source.

howToUse.title: Preview
howToUse.detail: Check how it reads against the surrounding paragraph.

howToUse.title: Save
howToUse.detail: Save the block.

whereToUse: A striking or quotable line worth pulling out of a long interview or feature.
Breaking up long stretches of body text for easier reading.
Emphasizing a key stat or claim mid-article.

blocks.tagline: A plain text link bounded by horizontal rules, used to promote an event or ticket sale within an article.
blocks.definition: A minimal callout consisting of a single underlined link — like an event ticket page — bounded above and below by thin horizontal divider rules.
blocks.howItWorks: The writer places a short, linked line of text at a natural break in the article, with divider rules above and below to visually separate it from the surrounding paragraphs.
whatIsExpected: A single line of underlined link text appears, bounded by divider rules above and below.
The link text is short and action-oriented (e.g. “Get your Moonshot 2026 ticket”).
Clicking the link takes the reader to the relevant event or ticket page.

whatIsExpected: The label “Read Next:” appears before the linked article title.
The block is bounded by divider rules above and below, matching the Event/Ticket Link style.
